title: Build a simple budget that balances income and expenses

lesson.title: Making a Budget That Balances

steps.say: You already know how to plan ahead to reach a savings goal, like saving a few dollars each week. Today we take one small step further: making a budget, which is a plan that shows where all of your money goes so that what you spend and save never adds up to more than what you get.

Let's meet Maya from Kelowna. In one week she gets twelve dollars allowance and earns eight dollars walking her neighbour's dog. Money that comes in is called income. Twelve dollars plus eight dollars is twenty dollars, so Maya's income for the week is twenty dollars.

visual.caption: Money coming in this week, in dollars

steps.say: Now Maya lists the things she plans to buy. Money that goes out is called expenses. She plans five dollars for bubble tea, seven dollars for a comic, and four dollars for bus fare. Five plus seven is twelve, and twelve plus four is sixteen. Her expenses are sixteen dollars.

visual.caption: Money going out this week, in dollars

steps.say: Here is the balancing part. Twenty dollars in, sixteen dollars out, so twenty minus sixteen leaves four dollars. That four dollars goes into her savings jar. Check it: sixteen dollars spent plus four dollars saved is exactly twenty dollars, the same as her income. When money out plus money saved equals money in, the budget balances.

visual.caption: Sixteen plus four equals twenty, so it balances

steps.say: Watch out for this mistake. Maya almost added a nine dollar movie ticket to her list. Sixteen plus nine is twenty five, but she only has twenty dollars coming in, so she would be short by five dollars. A budget is not balanced just because the list looks fun. The expenses must never be bigger than the income, so Maya keeps the movie for next week instead.

visual.caption: Twenty five dollars out is more than twenty dollars in, so this plan does not work

steps.say: So remember: add up your money in, add up your money out, and make sure what you spend plus what you save lands right back on what you earned.

lesson.answer: A budget balances when money out plus money saved equals money in.

practice.question: Noah lives in Victoria. This month he earns eighteen dollars babysitting and gets ten dollars allowance. He plans to spend twelve dollars on a skating pass and nine dollars on a birthday gift for his sister. Make a two column table on paper, one column for money in and one for money out. What is his total income, what are his total expenses, and how many dollars are left for his savings jar? Then check that his budget balances.
practice.answer: Income: eighteen plus ten equals twenty eight dollars. Expenses: twelve plus nine equals twenty one dollars. Left to save: twenty eight minus twenty one equals seven dollars. Check: twenty one dollars spent plus seven dollars saved equals twenty eight dollars, so the budget balances.
